scenes.title: Where and when
narration: The dance originates from the historical 'chumak' trade in Ukraine, where merchants traveled to the Black Sea and Crimea to trade goods for salt.
It serves as a choreographic record of this specific social class that existed from the 16th to the 19th centuries.
The dance captures the transition from the physical labor of the mines to the social life of the merchants.
on_screen: Map: Ukraine · Europe

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: Chumak is performed to celebrate Ukrainian heritage and the history of the salt trade.
It carries themes of hard work, resilience, and the joy of returning home.
It is a staple of both amateur folk festivals and professional ensemble performances.
Today it is a living tradition.

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: Dancers begin by interpreting the mining of salt from a cave through grounded, heavy movements.
This is followed by a sequence representing the desalination process.
The technique involves a mix of occupational mime and traditional Ukrainian folk steps.
Watch for The Salt Mine Mime, The Dramatic Fall.

scenes.title: The costume and the setting
narration: The traditional costume for a male dancer includes a straw hat, traditional Ukrainian clothes, and a belt.
The setting is often a stage or a village square, where the dancer can reenact the journey from the salt caves back to his home village.

scenes.title: The people
narration: One specific version features a young boy as the protagonist, focusing on his solo journey and a dramatic fall-and-recovery sequence, whereas other versions focus on the collective labor of a group of merchants.
Chumak is a subclass of Ukrainian folk dance, sharing the athletic and narrative characteristics of the broader regional tradition.
